subtopics.title: Rivers That Ignore the Rock — Superimposed and Antecedent Drainage

questions.question: In superimposed drainage, the river cuts across buried folds because it:
options: Was diverted by a lava flow
Developed its course on a younger rock cover and was lowered onto the older structure as the cover eroded away
Cut down faster than the land could rise
Follows a fault line through the mountains

questions.question: A river shows antecedent drainage when it:
options: Existed before uplift began and cut downward as fast as the land rose across its path
Was captured by a more powerful neighbour
Formed after the mountains were fully built
Reversed its direction of flow

questions.question: Both special patterns leave the same landform evidence, namely:
options: A wide floodplain with oxbow lakes
A radial pattern on a dome
A deep gorge where the river crosses high ground instead of flowing around it
A braided channel choked with sediment

questions.question: The single test that separates the two patterns is:
options: Which bank erodes faster
Whether the gorge holds water all year
How many tributaries join the river
Which is older — the river or the structure it crosses

subtopics.title: Why Catchments Matter — and Why They Are Poorly Managed

questions.question: The watershed of a drainage basin is:
options: The point where the river reaches the sea
The largest dam in the basin
The main channel of the river
The ridge of high ground separating the basin from its neighbours

questions.question: The governing principle of catchment management states that:
options: Everything done anywhere in the basin eventually registers in its river
Rivers purify themselves within ten kilometres
Only industries beside the channel affect water quality
Each municipality's water stays inside its boundary

questions.question: Durban's water security depends on land use far inland because the city draws its supply from:
options: Boreholes drilled beneath the city centre
The uMngeni system stepping down through Midmar, Albert Falls, Nagle and Inanda dams
Desalination plants along the coast
Direct pumping from the estuary

questions.question: Fragmented control damages catchments because:
options: Catchment agencies overrule the courts
Water law forbids municipalities from cooperating
The basin crosses administrative boundaries while each authority manages only its own fragment, so nobody owns the whole system
Basins are too large to map accurately

subtopics.title: Four Human Impacts — Pollution, Overgrazing, Deforestation, Settlement

questions.question: Which sequence gives the eutrophication chain in the correct order?
options: Bloom, nutrients in, oxygen crash, recovery
Oxygen crash, decomposition, bloom, nutrients in
Light blocked, bloom, nutrients in, suffocation
Nutrients in, algal bloom, light blocked, die-off, decomposition, oxygen crash and suffocation

questions.question: A South African dam repeatedly named for severe nutrient enrichment, blue-green blooms and hyacinth mats is:
options: Roodeplaat Dam, north of Pretoria
Katse Dam in Lesotho
Gariep Dam on the Orange
Woodstock Dam in the Drakensberg

questions.question: Overgrazing ultimately silts up dams because:
options: Livestock drink most of the streamflow
Crusted, bare soil sheds rapid runoff that strips topsoil into the channels
Animal waste fertilises the algae
Grazing compacts the dam wall itself

questions.question: Invasive alien trees such as black wattle are singled out in catchment studies because they:
options: Shade the water and cool it too much
Cannot hold soil on steep slopes
Transpire far more water than the indigenous vegetation they displaced, measurably shrinking streamflow
Produce seeds that poison fish

subtopics.title: Management Strategies and the Working for Wetlands Case Study

questions.question: National water law intends whole basins to be run by:
options: The largest municipality in each basin
Private irrigation boards
Provincial roads departments
Catchment management agencies bringing every user in the water management area around one table

questions.question: High ranges such as the Hottentots-Holland and Maloti-Drakensberg are called water factories because they:
options: Generate a disproportionate share of national runoff from a small share of the land
Host the country's biggest purification plants
Receive no rain but store snow
Contain most of the nation's boreholes

questions.question: The problem that Working for Wetlands attacks is:
options: Plastic pollution on beaches
Wetlands lost or degraded through draining, erosion gullies and development, robbing basins of their filters and sponges
Overfishing in inland dams
Acid mine drainage on the Witwatersrand

questions.question: The double dividend of Working for Wetlands is:
options: Cheaper electricity and faster transport
More timber and more grazing land
Restored wetland services — cleaner water, softer floods, steadier flow — plus jobs and training for poor rural communities
Higher dam walls and larger reservoirs

questions.question: In the funnel picture of a drainage basin, the rim of the funnel represents:
options: The watershed, where a raindrop must choose which river to join
The river mouth
The main dam wall
The floodplain

questions.question: The one commanding rule of the funnel is that:
options: Water always leaves the funnel as groundwater
Rain falls only on the rim
The funnel empties once a year
Whatever happens anywhere in the funnel ends up in the river

questions.question: A healthy funnel behaves like a sponge because:
options: Its dams release water on a schedule
Its wetlands and vegetated slopes absorb storms and release the water slowly
Its rivers flow underground
Its soil is naturally waterproof

questions.question: A river charging straight through a mountain range in a deep gorge was either lowered from a vanished cover or was older than the uplift — respectively called:
options: Radial and dendritic drainage
Trellis and braided drainage
Superimposed and antecedent drainage
Captured and rejuvenated drainage

subtopics.title: The Fish Tank That Turned Green

questions.question: In the over-fed fish tank story, the dissolved fish food represents:
options: Acid mine drainage
Plastic litter
Suspended silt
Nutrients — nitrates and phosphates from fertiliser, sewage and detergents

questions.question: The six beats of eutrophication in the correct order are:
options: Feed, bloom, dark, die, rot, suffocate
Bloom, feed, die, dark, suffocate, rot
Feed, dark, rot, bloom, die, suffocate
Die, rot, feed, bloom, dark, suffocate

questions.question: The fish in a eutrophied dam actually die because:
options: The algae sting them
Bacterial decomposition of the dead bloom strips the dissolved oxygen from the water
The water becomes too acidic to swim in
The hyacinth mats trap them underwater

questions.question: Cities make floods flashier because:
options: Urban rainfall is more intense than rural rainfall
Storm drains pump water uphill
Sealed tar and roofs cannot absorb rain, so storm water reaches the river within minutes
Bridges narrow every urban river

subtopics.title: Spades, Sponges and the Water Factories

questions.question: Wetlands earn the name sponges of the catchment because they:
options: Absorb flood peaks, filter pollutants and release water slowly through the dry season
Evaporate most of the water they receive
Store water only in summer
Prevent all erosion downstream

questions.question: A vegetated buffer strip along a river protects it by:
options: Marking the flood line for builders
Keeping livestock cool in summer
Blocking canoes and boats
Straining fertiliser and sediment out of runoff before it reaches the channel

questions.question: Working for Wetlands crews repair damaged wetlands by:
options: Dredging the wetland floor deeper
Plugging artificial drains, stopping gully head-cuts with gabions and concrete, and replanting indigenous cover
Spraying the wetland with herbicide
Building dams across the wetland outlet

questions.question: The five-sentence case-study answer for Working for Wetlands should contain:
options: The rainfall figures for every province it works in
The names of all the wetlands rehabilitated so far
The name, its two-decade track record, the wetland-loss problem, the spade-and-gabion method, and the double dividend of water services plus jobs
The budget totals for each financial year
